summary: Iteration 2 extends iteration 1. Backend: 20/20 new pytest cases pass covering DEMO/PILOT dataSource separation, pilot onboarding + status flip, WhatsApp unconfigured behavior (403 verify / 503 inbound / status badge), voice/status (Whisper configured=true), voice/transcribe graceful bad-audio handling, snapshot capture + history + comparison, markets/nearby sorted by distance, cron auth 401/200. Frontend: /whatsapp shows orange 'integration ready' badge + webhook contract + env vars; /business status & onboard tabs work; /network has capture-snapshot-button and snapshot-history; /vendor voice tab exposes vendor-mic-button; /join shopper flow submits and navigates to /shop with PILOT DATA badge shown. Code review confirms WhatsApp webhook uses conversation.process_message (single shared engine) — no duplicated AI logic. Iteration 1's 15 tests remain valid.

minor.issue: Could not verify a real speech transcript in this env (no TTS/ffmpeg available to synthesize audio). Endpoint handles malformed audio gracefully with ok=false and friendly error string — no stack trace. Recommend manual verification with a real .wav/.webm speech clip.

Endpoint correctly filters by dataSource. Was not strictly empty on a fresh call because a previous PILOT vendor signal remained from earlier iterations; separation logic itself is correct (DEMO pulse still returns full 8 products in parallel).

action_items: (Optional) Manually verify /api/voice/transcribe with a real short spoken .webm/.wav to close the last honesty check.
(Carry-over from iter-1, still open) Fix More.jsx hydration warning: <span> inside <option>.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:437 whatsapp_verify — verify_challenge uses hmac.compare_digest with an empty VERIFY_TOKEN which returns False, so any request 403s. Correct behavior for unconfigured env, but consider a distinct 503 (not-configured) vs 403 (bad token) so ops can tell them apart in production.

server.py:184 create_signal correctly tags dataSource from participantId; but there is no server-side validation that participantId actually exists in pilot_participants. A caller could pass any string and inflate PILOT metrics. Consider verifying against pilot_participants or at least logging unknown participantIds.

intelligence.capture_snapshot writes even when pulse.products is empty (the cron guards it, but /api/snapshots/capture does not) — allows empty PILOT snapshots to accumulate. Guard the direct endpoint too.

conversation.process_message hard-codes data_source='DEMO' for the pulse lookup on WhatsApp. Once pilots exist, WhatsApp shoppers will see DEMO pulse — pass a resolved data_source (based on the sender's participant record) into process_message.
voice_service.transcribe_audio uses NamedTemporaryFile with delete=True and re-opens by name — on some platforms this fails. Prefer delete=False + explicit unlink in finally.

server.py /api/pilot/status counts pilot_signals by dataSource=PILOT but 'Signal corroboration' display just says 'Live' regardless of count — not particularly meaningful. Consider surfacing the actual count.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend: /app/backend/tests/test_iteration2.py (20 tests) + /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (15 tests) all pass. Run with `-n 0` (xdist off) if you want serial execution. WhatsApp is intentionally unconfigured — 403 on verify and 503 on inbound are correct. Snapshot history accumulates each run; consider cleaning db.snapshot_history if it grows. If you need to test real Whisper transcription, generate a small speech .wav (e.g. via espeak or a TTS API) and POST it as multipart to /api/voice/transcribe — endpoint has been verified to handle both success and failure paths gracefully.
